content.title: Rizq Is Already Decreed, So Why So Much Anxiety?
content.subtitle: Anxiety cannot add a single drop that is not written in your destiny
content.body:
Have you ever woken up in the middle of the night with an unexplainable weight crushing your chest? Struggling to make ends meet at the end of the month or facing career uncertainty, do you ever feel like you just cannot keep going?

We are all chasing an invisible mirage. In pursuit of greater comfort, our days are consumed by exhaustion and dread. Yet how can we harbor doubts about the One who sustained us without fail for nine months in the pitch-black darkness of the womb—believing He would abandon us to starve under the open sky?

Settled Long Before Your Birth

Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: After 120 days of creation in the mother's womb, Allah sends an angel commanded to record four matters: “His deeds, his lifespan, his misery or happiness, and his provision.” (Sahih Bukhari: 3208, Sahih Muslim: 2643)

Long before you first saw the light of this world, the Lord of the Throne had precisely determined every single morsel you would ever consume. What has been decreed in the heavens, can any mortal on earth snatch away?

Provision Seeks You Even Faster Than Death

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ explicitly stated: “No created being shall die until it has completely received its decreed provision. So fear Allah and be moderate (seek through Halal means) in seeking provision. If provision is delayed, let no one be driven to seek it through disobedience to Allah (Haram).”

— (Mustadrak al-Hakim: 7873, Sunan Ibn Majah: 2144)

In another narration, the Prophet ﷺ remarked that a person's provision pursues them more relentlessly than death itself. Why, then, ruin your sleep night after night with crippling worry? Sincere effort is your responsibility, but the outcome rests entirely with your Lord.

The Trust of Birds and the Rush to the Forbidden

True trust in Allah (Tawakkul) does not mean sitting idle. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds—they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening full.” (Jami` at-Tirmidhi: 2344)

A bird does not perch passively on a branch; it spreads its wings at dawn to forage. Yet it never hoards food for tomorrow, nor does it suffer panic over what lies ahead. It knows that the One who fed it today will generously illuminate tomorrow’s dawn as well.

Abandoning Halal for Haram at the First Sign of Delay

Our greatest tragedy is our impatience. When a Halal door seems slow to open, business slows down, or honesty appears burdensome, the whisper arrives: “You are falling behind; everyone else takes shortcuts, so what harm is a little bribe or compromise?”

We forget: Haram can never increase our provision beyond what was already decreed. The wealth acquired through wrongful means was destined for you as Halal; through sheer impatience, you simply chose to swallow a pure blessing as poison.

Consider the severe warning in Sahih Muslim (Hadith: 1015): the disheveled traveler who lifts his hands to the sky crying, “O Lord! O Lord!” yet his food, drink, and clothing are Haram, nourished entirely by the unlawful. How could his prayer ever be answered?

Surrender Your Heart in Complete Reliance

In the Holy Quran, Allah Almighty grants us comfort: “And whoever fears Allah—He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.”

(Surah At-Talaq: 2–3)

Your hardship, your silent sighs, your silent tears—your Lord sees them all. Stand firm on righteousness, put forth your best effort, and pour out your heart in prostration. What is destined for you will reach you even carried by the wind; and what was never yours cannot be held, no matter how desperately you weep.
